items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:27:1
items.html:
That the light become distant from it by three degrees: For a vessel is not made except by the departure of the light from her entirely, both inner light and surrounding light. And it is known that up to two degrees the vessel still receives surrounding light, and therefore it does not become a vessel until the light becomes distant from it by three degrees. For, for example, the vessel of ZA: at the time when the light of ZA departs from the vessel and rises to Bina, this is not yet counted as a distance of a degree, since it still receives Yechida of the inner light; rather only at the time when it becomes distant and rises to Hochma does it become distant from the vessel by one degree, and it receives the first surrounding light; and afterward, when it becomes distant by two degrees and rises to Keter, behold, it receives also the second surrounding light. And behold, the vessel has still not darkened entirely until it departs also from Keter to the Emanator, whereupon the vessel attains no light whatever and it is completed.
And likewise the vessel of Malchut: when the light becomes distant from her by one degree — that is, when the light of Malchut rises to ZA — behold, she still receives the first surrounding light; and when it becomes distant by two degrees, that is, at the time it rises to Bina, behold, she still receives the second surrounding light; but at the time when the light of Malchut rises to Hochma, which is the third degree, she already receives no illumination whatever. And then the vessel of Malchut darkens and is completed.
And therefore from Bina upward the vessels were not completed. For even when the light of Bina rises to Keter, behold, Bina still receives the Yechida of the inner light, which is not discerned at all as a distance of a degree. And all the more so Keter and Hochma. And see all this in the words of the ARI above (Part 4, Chapter 6, item 15) and in all that follows there.
And besides the above, there is another condition for the completion of a vessel, which is the completion of the outer half of the wall in the vessel, as above in the words of the ARI (Part 4, Chapter 4, item 3): that as long as there is no outer half of the wall in the vessel, which belongs to the reception of surrounding lights, the vessel is not completed. And behold, the vessels of GAR attained no surrounding lights at the time of their ascent to the Emanator, as written there in the words of the ARI; and the vessels of GAR are found lacking the outer half of the wall of their vessels, and they were therefore not completed except afterward in the second expansion. As the ARI says here.
